events.title: The Guardian publishes an op-ed written by GPT-3
events.summary: On 8 September 2020 The Guardian ran a column headlined “A robot wrote this entire article. Are you scared yet, human?” Editors asked GPT-3 to argue, in about 500 plain words, that people have nothing to fear from AI. Liam Porr, a UC Berkeley computer science student, fed the paper’s prompts to the model, which returned eight different essays. Opinion editor Amana Fontanella-Khan then cut and rearranged the strongest passages into the published piece, and noted the edit took less time than many human op-eds.
events.imageAlt: A newspaper page with a short column, a pull quote, and a small geometric robot finishing a line with a pen.

events.title: OpenAI shares mathematical results from a frontier model
events.summary: On 6 October 2026 OpenAI said it was releasing a broad set of new mathematical results from an internal frontier model, in a GitHub repository with revision and citation protocols, Lean formalizations of many proofs, ten summaries of the model’s reasoning, and compute notes. The average result used about three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking. The lab said the release followed advice from the Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence at the Institute for Advanced Study. On 15 October it added a $5 million contribution, awarded by the Simons Foundation, for workshops and programs so mathematicians can examine and extend those results, plus model and compute access for supported researchers.
events.imageAlt: A triangle inscribed in a circle beside a proof card whose last line is marked checked.
